findings.description: `testRunsElsewhere` only checks that something exists at `~/.pupitre/slots`, then reads it and calls `waitingGates`. That function unlinks every `*.wait` entry it reads as dead (unparseable, a symlink, not a regular file, or a dead pid). The gate runs it unsandboxed, outside any session sandbox. Before this PR the gate never called `waitingGates`: `acquire` passes `[]` for a gate. So a session that swaps the slots directory for a link to another directory can now get the trusted gate to delete `*.wait` files there, plus `slot-N.lock` names via `reclaim`, which the gate's `acquire` already followed. ADR 0096 says sessions can write this path. Impact is minimal, since the reachable damage is limited to files with those exact names. Treating anything that is not a directory as "a run is going" (`if (!entry.isDirectory()) return true;` after the lstat) would also match ADR 0134's rule that anything it cannot treat as the slots directory counts as a run.

When `testRunsElsewhere` returns true only because its catch fired (the slots path is a file, a dangling link, or unreadable), the wait line still says "while other test runs are going". It should say the slots could not be read.

"as every reader of the slots does" overstates. Only `acquire` and `testRunsElsewhere` call `liveHolders`. It also omits that a dead gate's wait file is removed (`waitingGates`). Suggestion: replace the last sentence with "A dead holder's slot is reclaimed and a dead gate's wait file removed, as `acquire` does." The same overstatement is in docs/adr/0134-the-gate-waits-for-the-load-only-while-another.md line 27.

Line 36 runs two sentences together and wraps well past the ~100-column wrap every other line of the ADR keeps ('...which already counts. Load from a worker's Claude session, which takes no slot, no longer holds a'). Re-wrap it, and the ragged Tests paragraph at lines 43-46, to match the neighbouring ADRs.

"(security review of a4545ff)" cites a bare commit hash. It will not resolve after a squash merge and gives a reader no context. Suggestion: describe the review finding in prose, or drop the citation.

"the load is none of pup's tests, which the wait cannot outlast" has an unclear antecedent. "Which" could mean the load or the tests. Suggestion: "with none, the load is not pup's tests' doing and waiting cannot clear it, so the gate runs at once".

The `othersGoing` comment says "holds a test slot", but the stub stands for `testRunsElsewhere`, which also covers a live gate wait file. Suggestion: "/** Stands for `testRunsElsewhere` answering true: the load may be pup's. */"

The title says "only while another test run is going", but the rule also keeps the wait when the slots path is unreadable, so a wait can happen with no run going. The ADR body does state this, so the title is just loose.

`testRunsElsewhere` is a read-only-sounding predicate that calls `liveHolders` (reclaims dead holders' slots) and `waitingGates` (deletes dead waiters' files), and builds a throwaway `randomBytes` token only to name the reclaim file; the JSDoc discloses the reclaim, but the side effect hides behind a predicate name and the token arguably belongs inside `liveHolders`.

The `options: Pick<TestSlotOptions, 'dir' | 'slots'>` parameter is used only by the new tests in `test-slot.test.ts`; the production caller, `waitForLoad`, passes nothing. It mirrors the existing `withTestSlot` dir/slots seam, so it is borderline under AGENTS.md §Altitude.

The new "with the machine's own test slots" cases for `waitForLoad`'s default path partly repeat the `testRunsElsewhere` unit tests in `test-slot.test.ts`, adding mostly wiring coverage of the default argument, and rely on `process.ppid` being alive as the foreign holder.
